what_its_for: Nortriptyline is used to treat depression. It may also be used for nerve pain, bedwetting in children, and sometimes to help people quit smoking. It belongs to a group of medicines called tricyclic antidepressants, which work by balancing certain natural chemicals in your brain to improve mood and feelings of well-being.
how_to_take: Take nortriptyline by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a small snack or glass of milk. It is often taken once a day at bedtime because it can cause drowsiness, but your doctor may tell you to split the doses throughout the day. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the capsule. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it to find the right amount for you. For adults, the typical dose ranges from 25 mg to 150 mg per day. For older adults and teenagers, doses are usually lower, often 30 mg to 50 mg per day. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause unpleasant withdrawal effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store nortriptyline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the container tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine that is past its expiration date. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking nortriptyline, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may worsen side effects. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting up too quickly from sitting or lying down, as this medicine can cause a drop in blood pressure that may make you feel dizzy or faint. Avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight or tanning beds, as nortriptyline can make your skin more sensitive to the sun. Do not take any new prescription or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as many medicines can interact with nortriptyline. Do NOT take MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine or selegiline) within 14 days of taking nortriptyline, as this combination can cause a dangerous reaction.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: thoughts of hurting yourself or suicide, new or worsening depression or anxiety, unusual changes in mood or behavior, chest pain or irregular heartbeat, difficulty urinating, severe constipation, signs of a serious allergic reaction (rash, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing), seizures, or a very high fever with confusion and stiff muscles. Also call your doctor if you have blurred vision, dry mouth, dizziness when standing, or any side effects that bother you or do not go away. IMPORTANT: Antidepressants may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts, especially in children, teenagers, and young adults during the first few weeks of treatment. Contact your doctor immediately if this occurs.
when_it_works: Nortriptyline does not work right away. It may take 2 to 4 weeks before you start to feel better, and sometimes up to 6 to 8 weeks to feel the full benefit. Do not stop taking it just because you do not feel better right away. Keep taking it as prescribed and let your doctor know if you do not notice any improvement after a few weeks.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Use during pregnancy should only be considered if the benefit outweighs the risk. BREASTFEEDING: Nortriptyline passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. OLDER ADULTS: Older adults are more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially dizziness, drowsiness, confusion, and falls. Lower doses are usually recommended. CHILDREN: This medicine is generally not recommended for children under 12 years for depression. It may be used for bedwetting in children 6 years and older under close medical supervision. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. HEART CONDITIONS: Tell your doctor if you have any heart problems before starting this medicine, as nortriptyline can affect heart rhythm.
